# A Note on AI Assistance {.unnumbered}

Every chapter of this book was researched, written, and rewritten by me. However, I want to be entirely transparent about how the use of AI tools in *Volume 4: Physical AI* differed from their use in my previous volumes.

In the *Machine Learning Systems* volume, I knew exactly what I was doing; the systems and infrastructure domain is my native intellectual home. There, AI acted primarily as a force multiplier---writing code, standardizing notation, and auditing cross-references. 

In this volume on Physical AI, it was a bit different. I had to use AI to learn parts of this discipline myself. Moving from silicon accelerators to kinematic chains, real-time control barrier functions, and physical contact mechanics required me to cross into mechanical engineering, control theory, and robotics. I had to be a student again to figure these things out. I leaned on large language models as interactive tutors to explain unfamiliar dynamics, trace derivations from classical control literature, and pressure-test my understanding. Because I was synthesizing concepts outside my core expertise, I also relied heavily on external verification from domain experts---human roboticists and control engineers---to rigorously vet the concepts I had developed with AI assistance. 

What follows is a statement of the standard I held the book to, and a claim about what authorship means in an era of highly capable AI tutors.

The standard is traceability. Derived quantities in these chapters are backed by Python computation cells. Citations were checked against their sources, and the foundational math was rigorously checked against established textbooks. AI tools made the learning and the synthesis tractable, and the enforcement infrastructure made the result auditable.

Authorship is thinking and taking responsibility. Which concepts belong in this book and which do not. How to sequence the chapters so that each idea arrives only after the reader has the tools to understand it. I used AI tools throughout this process to accelerate my own learning and to draft passages, which I then rewrote and externally verified. The choices, the synthesis, and the final intellectual product are mine.

The tool can propose, and the tool can even tutor, but only the human engineer can ratify and assume responsibility.
